ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0069 concerns the corpus's use of Indigenous intellectual lineage and was read before restoring the Haudenosaunee passage. The shipped requirement that the tradition not be borrowed as a slogan and that any use carry accurate history, attribution, and attention to the communities it comes from is kept in full. CTD-0078 requires that research lineage not function as proof, which bears on the Welsh and Dasgupta citations. CTD-0007 governs epigraph attribution.

findings.summary: The failure mode was named and its direction removed.

evidence.baseline: The primary temporal failure mode is not the neglect of any single layer but the colonization of longer-timeframe layers by shorter-timeframe pressures.
evidence.shipped: Short clocks often consume long ones.

findings.authorizedBy: Catalog 4.3 applied to the not X but Y construction.
findings.diagnosis: Short clocks consume long ones is a good compact image and is kept in the restoration. What it cannot carry is the correction: the reader's natural assumption is that the danger is neglecting a layer, and the chapter's claim is that the danger is one layer eating another. 4.3's retention limb applies because the rejected alternative is the one a reader arrives holding, and the whole design of protective mechanisms follows from the corrected claim.

findings.summary: The bidirectional requirement, which is what stops the chapter from arguing for pure entrenchment, was cut to a sentence.

evidence.baseline: These mechanisms work in both directions: they protect longer-timeframe layers from colonization by shorter-timeframe pressures, and they prevent longer-timeframe commitments from becoming so rigid that they cannot be adapted when shorter-timeframe experience reveals that adaptation is needed.
evidence.shipped: Providence therefore needs boundaries between temporal layers, plus a lawful way to revise them. Long commitments need protection from convenience. Present experience needs a way to correct the past.

findings.diagnosis: The shipped three sentence version is close and is kept. The baseline states the requirement as one mechanism working two ways rather than as two separate needs, which matters because the chapter's Open Questions return to it as a single unresolved tension rather than as two solved problems. Both formulations are in the restoration.

reasoning.note: R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Five em dashes in the section and its following interlude. Three were parenthetical and became comma pairs. One introduced the enumeration of protective mechanisms and became a colon. One in the interlude introduced a specification of what the economics is for and became a colon.
The shipped sentence that inherited rules can preserve mistakes and the shipped requirement that each safeguard have a release valve. Both are additions the baseline lacks.
The colonization claim with its correction, the four instances of colonization, the bidirectional requirement, and the four named protective mechanisms in their full form.

The Part II interlude in full. The shipped text kept only its first sentence, which the voice card protects as The long clock matters only if people can live inside it. The restored interlude opens on that protected line and continues into the baseline's account of what the economic architecture is for.

openQuestions: The section's measured word count now exceeds the baseline's by a wide margin. This is a measurement artifact rather than an inflation: the damage tool splits on markdown headings, and with the coda headings gone this section absorbs the Part II opener that the baseline assigned to the coda. The same artifact affects six other sections in this volume.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

The heading is the shipped one, not the baseline's. Baseline headings were not restored because `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records the rename and resolves the historical route, and this pass has no standing to add lineage entries. Where the baseline heading names the section better, that is recorded in the finding and left for the author.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The section closes Part I and carries the protected line whose paragraph the pass removed, which is the same pattern recorded at the nest in the orientation. Two protected lines left standing without their paragraphs is the volume's signature on this pass.
